title: TESS data to sector 107 show repeat transits for six single-transit TOIs with no published period and limit the periods of 58 other single-transit TOIs
abstract: We searched all public TESS light curves (SPOC 2-min, TESS-SPOC and QLP; sectors 1-107; 2,982 files) of the 109 TESS Objects of Interest that have a catalog period of 0. For each TOI we moved a box of the catalog duration across the data, with a local sideband baseline and an empirical SNR. We vetted each dip of SNR 7 or more in a second pipeline and by depth, duration and background. We also calculated which periods the non-detections remove, with a conservative depth. All 22 published periods in the sample are inside the allowed sets; one published period was removed by our first rule, and we changed the rule after this failure. We recovered second transits of TOI-561 e, HD 152843 c, TOI-2447 b and NGTS-30 b, and the alias set of TOI-2490.01 contains its published 60.33-day period. Six TOIs with no published period show repeat events. TOI-3500.02 has two new transits in 2025 and 2026, which leave nine periods (18.4-350.3 d). TOI-790.03 has a second 17-hour transit in 2025, which leaves 363.4 or 726.9 d. TOI-6663.01, TOI-2534.01 and TOI-6667.01 have new events that leave 14, 27 and 5 aliases. The repeating dips of TOI-6890.01 are 734.7/n days apart, and its catalog event is probably a sector-start artefact. For 58 TOIs with a reliable catalog event, TESS removes all periods below a median of 30.5 days. Dip and brightening events occur at similar rates, so SNR alone does not confirm an event. We did no pixel-level vetting, so eclipsing binaries remain possible, and strict-period exclusion fails when transit times vary.

display.caption: All accepted transit events of six single-transit TOIs with no published period. Each panel shows one event in the best pipeline (SPOC 2-min, TESS-SPOC or QLP), normalised by a local linear baseline (grey: data; points: 30-min bins). Blue marks the catalog event and orange the other events. The aqua band is the catalog duration.

Orbital periods that agree with all accepted events and with all TESS non-detections (dots), for six new multi-event systems (orange) and four validation systems with published periods (blue; black tick: published period). The aqua bar is the circular-orbit period range for impact parameter 0 to 0.9, from the catalog duration and stellar density. It is for context only.

Allowed (aqua) and excluded (grey) periods from 3 to 3,000 days for 58 single-transit TOIs with a catalog event of SNR 8 or more, from all TESS data to sector 107. Black ticks are published periods; orange dots are aliases allowed by confirmed repeat events.
